definition: Source states that a company develops, markets or provides a named product; action stage retained separately.
temporal_rules: Explicit product launch or offering period; unknown beginning remains unknown
positive_examples: Company explicitly names its product offering.
counterexamples: Company and product mentioned in one article without ownership/offering link.
evidence_requirements: Explicit source statement; both entity IDs; direction/roles; product scope; modality; dates; auditable evidence location
selection_reason: Company-product scope supports product event comparison.

definition: Source states that a company offers a named service; offering stage and conditions remain separate.
temporal_rules: Explicit service offering/effective period; past state not inferred
positive_examples: Company explicitly names its service offering.
counterexamples: Use of another firm service as evidence of ownership.
evidence_requirements: Explicit source statement; both entity IDs; direction/roles; product scope; modality; dates; auditable evidence location
selection_reason: Service scope supports financial and product event separation.

definition: Source explicitly states a company collaboration with a named company; no customer/supplier role implied.
temporal_rules: Publication and effective interval retained; plans not current relationship
positive_examples: Named partnership statement with project context.
counterexamples: Co-mention or common market described as a partnership.
evidence_requirements: Explicit source statement; both entity IDs; direction/roles; product scope; modality; dates; auditable evidence location
selection_reason: Nonquantitative business change must be preserved without invented revenue.

definition: Source explicitly states provision of a stated product/service by supplier to named customer, preserving sample/commercial stage.
temporal_rules: Plan and executed shipments distinct; source validity interval required
counterexamples: Unnamed concentrated customer guessed from market share.
evidence_requirements: Explicit source statement; both entity IDs; direction/roles; product scope; modality; dates; auditable evidence location
selection_reason: Candidate only until an explicit source gives counterpart and scope.

definition: Source explicitly identifies competition within a defined product/service market.
positive_examples: Explicit company competitor list with market scope.
counterexamples: Both firms listed in an industry news article.
evidence_requirements: Explicit source statement; both entity IDs; direction/roles; product scope; modality; dates; auditable evidence location
selection_reason: Candidate; no competition conclusion from ticker sector or co-occurrence.

definition: A company presents a named reporting segment in its financial segment table. The stated reporting period and presentation definition bound the claim.
scope_constraints: reported_segment_only; neither ownership legal proof nor product/customer/supplier relationship
temporal_rules: Source reference/reporting period only; creation/termination and ongoing validity unknown.
positive_examples: Company segment-revenue table names a reporting segment under an explicit reporting period.
counterexamples: A segment name used as a product revenue alias or named customer.
evidence_requirements: Named segment row plus segment table caption and reporting-period header; both stable entity IDs.
selection_reason: Preserve company-versus-segment scope and presentation changes without sales-impact inference.
